policies.title: S3 public access must be blocked
policies.description: Amazon S3 buckets must enable all four Public Access Block controls so anonymous or unexpected public access cannot be introduced through ACLs or bucket policies.
policies.control_objective: Prevent unintended public exposure of cloud storage objects and bucket listings.

policies.title: S3 default encryption must be configured
policies.description: Buckets must declare a compliant default server-side encryption configuration (AES256 or KMS). ASPARe records the modern S3 baseline-encryption caveat: AWS may encrypt new objects even when GetBucketEncryption reports no explicit customer configuration.
policies.control_objective: Ensure objects inherit an explicit, policy-approved server-side encryption configuration.

policies.title: S3 versioning must be enabled
policies.description: Object versioning must be enabled so accidental deletes or overwrites can be recovered. Default risk policy alerts rather than auto-remediates this medium-severity control.
policies.control_objective: Preserve object history and support recovery from destructive changes.

policies.title: S3 must enforce HTTPS (TLS) in transit
policies.description: The bucket policy must contain an explicit Deny for requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, covering the bucket ARN and object ARNs.
policies.control_objective: Prevent unencrypted transport of storage API requests and object data.

policies.title: S3 ACLs must not grant public or authenticated-user access
policies.description: Bucket ACLs must not grant AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers permissions. Buckets using BucketOwnerEnforced object ownership have ACLs disabled and are treated as compliant for this control.
policies.control_objective: Eliminate public ACL exposure of cloud storage.
